newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends flat, shrugs off JGB rally.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends flat, shrugs off JGB rally.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures ended Friday's TIFFE day session flat despite a rally in the Japanese government bond (JGB) market.
The December settled at 99.22, after trading between 99.20 and 99.24. Turnover was 41,794 contracts.
"The Euroyen futures market showed little reaction to the sharp rise in JGBs, as players saw it as a technically-driven rally," said a city bank trader.
Key June JGB futures closed up 0.45 at 126.70. The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB fell to a record-low of 2.190 percent at one point, from 2.240 percent on Thursday.
"Some short-covering was seen in Euroyen futures, but selling pressure was quite strong," the trader said.
The December hit an intraday high of 99.24 earlier in the day on expectations that the Nikkei would fall sharply following an overnight plunge in New York stocks, traders said.
However, the rise was short-lived as stocks pared losses.
The Nikkei 225 stock average closed up 23.16 points, or 0.13 percent, at 17,923.64, after falling as low as 17,616.79.
